If unstable, peritoneal signs, severe unilateral pain, syncope, fever, cervical motion/adnexal/uterine tenderness, or concern for ectopic pregnancy or tubo-ovarian abscess is present, urgent emergency/gynecologic evaluation and imaging are required; do not wait for vaginitis or STI results.

entities.name: Acute pelvic pain
observations: In a sexually active reproductive-age patient, acute abdominal or pelvic pain requires pregnancy testing to evaluate pregnancy-related emergencies, particularly ectopic pregnancy.
Thin foul-smelling discharge and itching warrant subsequent vaginitis testing and STI testing, but these do not replace pregnancy assessment.

source_tools.relevance: Supports prioritizing pregnancy testing in acute pelvic pain
Supports urgent exclusion of pregnancy-related emergencies

entities.name: Ectopic pregnancy
observations: Must be excluded promptly in a sexually active patient of reproductive age with acute abdominal or pelvic pain; urine hCG is the appropriate initial screen.

source_tools.relevance: Supports pregnancy testing before attributing pain to vaginitis
Supports hCG priority in acute pelvic pain

entities.name: Urine hCG
observations: Point-of-care urine hCG is the highest-priority single test in this scenario; a positive result directs urgent quantitative serum beta-hCG and pelvic ultrasound evaluation.

source_tools.relevance: Supports urine hCG as first step

entities.name: Vaginitis symptoms
observations: Foul-smelling thin discharge and itching are compatible with bacterial vaginosis or trichomoniasis, while itching can also occur with candidiasis; symptoms alone do not reliably distinguish causes.
Vaginal pH, saline wet mount, and KOH/whiff testing are complementary bedside tests after or concurrently with pregnancy assessment.

source_tools.relevance: Supports differential diagnosis and test sequence
Supports limitations and role of wet mount and bedside testing

entities.name: Pelvic inflammatory disease
observations: Pelvic pain plus abnormal discharge in a sexually active adolescent warrants prompt STI testing, including chlamydia and gonorrhea NAAT; testing should not delay empiric treatment when minimum clinical criteria are met.

source_tools.relevance: Supports prompt evaluation and treatment principles
